data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in the Czech Republic performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed relative to earlier PISA cycles (notably 2018 and longer trends since 2000). The assessment uses two two-hour subject tests with different students receiving different combinations of test questions, plus a student background questionnaire and a school principal questionnaire. The factsheet reports mean performance trends, the distribution of students across proficiency levels (e.g., Level 2 and Level 5/6), and gaps by socio-economic status (ESCS quintiles and top/bottom 25%), gender, and several school-life indicators (belonging, discipline, safety, bullying, parental involvement). For the Czech Republic, average mathematics performance declined versus 2018, while reading and science were about the same as in 2018; in mathematics, the share below Level 2 increased, and the share at Level 5/6 was 11%. The document also notes that PISA 2021 was delayed to 2022 due to COVID-19 and that some countries may have sampling-standard issues (marked with an asterisk), while the Czech Republic met quality standards.
